name: Harness memory recall
description: Recalls what this deployment remembers and prepends its structure to a turn's context.

read.title: Reader argv
read.description: The reader to spawn, as argv, up to and including the `bundle` subcommand. Written by harnesses/openclaw/install-memory.sh. An argv that is empty, or that names a read shape other than `bundle`, recalls nothing and says so in the log rather than injecting silence.

threadEntity.title: Thread entity kind
threadEntity.description: The entity kind this deployment files conversations under, as its spec/entities.yaml declares it. Set it and a turn inside a thread looks that thread up; leave it unset and no thread is asked about. There is no default, because an entity vocabulary belongs to the deployment rather than to this harness.

actors.title: Agent id to writer name
actors.description: This deployment's map from the host's agent id to the writer name that agent's records were filed under — for example {"main": "main_bot"}. The two are named separately on purpose: a record carries whatever caller its record socket signed as, so the writer name belongs to the keyring and this plugin cannot derive it from an agent id. An agent this map does not name asks about no actor at all, and says so in the log; passing the agent id instead would ask about a writer that never wrote anything and return a page indistinguishable from a quiet store.

actorMaxRecords.title: Background rows the actor may carry
actorMaxRecords.description: Most rows of an answer that may be the asking agent's own recent activity rather than an answer to the message. The actor is a background source: it fills what the entities left, up to this many, and it carries nothing at all on a turn whose entities matched nothing — a page of one agent's week is the same page whatever was asked, and a turn with no answer must not be given one that only looks like it. Set it to 0 for a deployment that wants no background page. Zero means zero here, not "use the default".

specDir.title: Entity spec directory
specDir.description: The deployment's spec directory, holding entities.yaml and extractors.yaml. Set it and the turn's message is read for entity references, which are looked up alongside the thread and the actor. Read-time inference only: a key guessed wrongly matches nothing, and the confidence a stored reference needs to reach a bundle is untouched.

timeoutMs.title: Recall budget (ms)
timeoutMs.description: How long the whole lookup gets. It sits in front of a reply, so a slow read is a slow conversation: when it runs out the turn proceeds with no recalled context.

maxRecords.title: Records injected
maxRecords.description: Most records one turn may carry. Also the reader's `--limit`, so a turn that wants eight records is charged for eight rather than for the service's cap.

maxChars.title: Characters injected
maxChars.description: Ceiling on the rendered block. Whatever it cuts is counted in the block, because a truncated list that reads as complete is worse than a short one.

searchFallback.title: Search when the bundle matched nothing
searchFallback.description: A bundle that matched nothing is followed by one ranked search over the same socket, injected under a heading saying it is the weaker claim. Set it false for a deployment that wants only what its keys support. Declared here because the host refuses a config key this schema does not name: an undeclared setting is not a default, it is a config the gateway will not load.

digestDays.title: Session-opening digest window (days)
digestDays.description: Days of recent activity a session wakes up holding, as a date-grouped digest. Injected on the turn that opens a session, and only where the turn's own entities matched nothing — a composed answer keeps the space, a ranked search does not, and neither does the actor's background page, which is why the actor is never asked for on a turn that has no answer to supplement. Unset is off, and off is the default: a digest says who acted, when, and what they referenced, and never what any of it was about — whether that reads as background or as noise depends on a store this harness has not seen.

digestMaxRecords.title: Digest rows
digestMaxRecords.description: Most rows a digest may carry, and the window read's `--limit`. Wider than maxRecords by default, because a digest is a list rather than an answer.

digestMaxChars.title: Digest characters
digestMaxChars.description: Ceiling on the rendered digest, and it belongs below maxChars. A window read returns a window rather than a match, so it is the likelier of the two to be cut — and whatever it cuts is counted in the block.

record.title: Agent id to recorder argv
record.description: This deployment's map from the host's agent id to that agent's own record tool, as argv up to and including the program — for example {"main": ["/usr/local/bin/record-main"]}. Set it alongside recordAction and a turn that ran without recording anything gets a floor record from a post-turn hook. Per agent because a record carries whatever caller its socket signed as: another agent's recorder would file the turn under a writer that did not do it, so an agent this map does not name records nothing and says so. The argv may carry only the flags saying who is writing and where — --socket, --agent, --agent-ver, --redaction-policy, --timeout-ms — and one naming anything else records nothing at all. Everything a record says is built by the hook, which is what keeps a subject off that line rather than merely unlikely on it.

recordAction.title: Action a turn is recorded as
recordAction.description: The action name this deployment's attribute schema declares for an agent turn. There is no default, because a store refuses a record whose action it never declared — so a name invented here would be a rejected write on every turn. Unset is off, and off is the default; set without config.record it stays off, because an action with no recorder writes nowhere.

recordOutcomes.title: Turn outcome to declared outcome
recordOutcomes.description: How this deployment spells the two outcomes a post-turn hook can tell apart, as {"success": "success", "failure": "failure"} — which is also the default. A store refuses a record whose action does not declare the outcome it carries, so where an action has no word for one of the two, set that entry to the empty string and turns of that kind are not recorded at all. Filing a failed turn as a success because the schema had nowhere else to put it is the one thing this must not do: no later read could tell.

recordAttrs.title: Hook fact to declared attribute key
recordAttrs.description: Which of the two facts a post-turn hook has reach the record, and under which of this deployment's declared attribute keys — as {"channel": "channel", "recalled": "recalled"}. Only `channel`, the conversation the turn ran in, and `recalled`, whether recall put anything in front of it, are understood; anything else is warned about at load and never sent, because a key this hook cannot fill would look wired. Unset sends no attributes, which is the working default: a record with none is accepted everywhere, and one carrying a key its action did not declare is refused on every turn.

recordTimeoutMs.title: Recording budget (ms)
recordTimeoutMs.description: How long the record write gets. It sits behind a reply rather than in front of one, so it can be generous where the recall budget cannot: the turn has already finished, and the host neither waits for this hook nor lets it fail a turn. When it runs out nothing is recorded and the log says so.
